This reference covers all **159 YAML parameters and containers** in
BonVoyage configuration schema version **1**. The
tables are generated from the release-matched completion metadata and reviewed
field-help catalog. The examples come from the compiler-backed snippet catalog.

:::tip[Start with a complete document]
Use the [Docker quickstart](../../getting-started/quickstart/) and the baseline
below before adding optional transport, policy, or routing fragments.
:::

## How to read the paths

Paths use RFC 6901-style notation. A `*` represents one array item, so
`/listeners/*/port` means the `port` field on every object in the
top-level `listeners` array.

`Required` means the field is directly required by its containing object.
`Optional` fields can still become conditionally required by another selection.
Those relationships are listed under [cross-field rules](#cross-field-rules).
Exact regular expressions and structural rules remain available in
`config/schemas/bonvoyage-config.schema.json`. The authoritative
Go snapshot compiler performs semantic validation, defaults, reference checks,
and supported-feature checks that a field table cannot replace.

## Complete baseline example

**Local gateway baseline.** Start a complete local listener, fixed response, proxied route, upstream cluster and bounded runtime profile.

`config/examples/local.yaml`:

```yaml
server:
  node_id: bonvoyage-local
  admin_addr: 127.0.0.1:9901
  metrics_addr: 127.0.0.1:9090
snapshot:
  schema_version: 1
  snapshot_id: local-bootstrap
  generation: 1
  minimum_dataplane_version: 0.2.0
listeners:
  - name: http
    address: 0.0.0.0
    port: 8080
    protocol: http1
    virtual_hosts:
      - default
virtual_hosts:
  - name: default
    domains:
      - '*'
    routes:
      - name: local-response
        match:
          path_exact: /bonvoyage/ready
        fixed_response:
          status_code: 200
          body: |
            ready
          content_type: text/plain
      - name: default-route
        match:
          path_prefix: /
        cluster: local-upstream
clusters:
  - name: local-upstream
    load_balancing_policy: round_robin
    connect_timeout_ms: 1000
    max_connections_per_shard: 128
    max_pending_requests_per_shard: 256
    endpoints:
      - name: upstream-1
        address: upstream
        port: 8081
        weight: 1
runtime_limits:
  max_downstream_connections_per_shard: 16384
  max_request_header_bytes: 32768
  max_request_body_bytes: 10485760
  max_upstream_response_header_bytes: 32768
  max_upstream_chunk_metadata_bytes: 32768
  request_timeout_ms: 15000
  downstream_idle_timeout_ms: 60000
```

Validate the complete file before applying it:

```bash
go run ./control-plane/cmd/bonvoyage-config validate \
  --input config/examples/local.yaml
```

## Feature examples

Each fragment below names its insertion path. Merge it into a complete document,
then validate the whole document. Secret-reference fields accept deployment
filenames such as `server-key.pem`; never paste a private key,
API key, JWKS document, or certificate body into YAML.

<details id="example-cluster-upstream-mtls">
<summary>Upstream TLS and mTLS</summary>

Add server identity verification and an optional client certificate to one upstream cluster.

Place this fragment at `/clusters/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
upstream_tls:
  server_name: backend.internal.example.com
  trust_bundle_secret: backend-ca.pem
  certificate_chain_secret: gateway-client.pem
  private_key_secret: gateway-client-key.pem
```

</details>

<details id="example-listener-downstream-tls">
<summary>Downstream TLS</summary>

Enable a listener certificate and private-key reference using deployment-secret filenames.

Place this fragment at `/listeners/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
downstream_tls:
  certificate_chain_secret: server-chain.pem
  private_key_secret: server-key.pem
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-api-key-auth">
<summary>API-key admission</summary>

Require a named request header whose value is checked against a deployment-secret credential file.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
api_key_auth:
  header_name: X-API-Key
  credentials_secret: phase3-api-keys.txt
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-cors">
<summary>CORS policy</summary>

Add bounded browser-origin, method, header, credential and preflight-cache rules to one route.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
cors:
  allowed_origins:
    - https://app.example.com
    - http://localhost:3000
  allowed_methods:
    - GET
  allowed_headers:
    - Authorization
    - Content-Type
    - X-Request-Id
  exposed_headers:
    - X-Request-Id
    - X-Trace-Id
  allow_credentials: true
  max_age_seconds: 600
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-fixed-response">
<summary>Fixed-response route</summary>

Append a route that returns a local status, body and content type without contacting an upstream.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes` using `append-array-item` semantics:

```yaml
- name: local-response
  match:
    path_exact: /bonvoyage/ready
  fixed_response:
    status_code: 200
    body: |
      ready
    content_type: text/plain
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-header-transformations">
<summary>Header transformations</summary>

Set, append or remove bounded request and response headers on one route.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
header_transformations:
  request:
    - operation: set
      name: x-request-set
      value: gateway-set
    - operation: append
      name: x-request-append
      value: gateway-append
    - operation: remove
      name: x-request-remove
    - operation: set
      name: x-request-added
      value: gateway-added
  response:
    - operation: set
      name: x-response-set
      value: gateway-set
    - operation: append
      name: x-response-append
      value: gateway-append
    - operation: remove
      name: x-response-remove
    - operation: set
      name: x-response-added
      value: gateway-added
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-jwt-auth">
<summary>JWT admission</summary>

Validate JWT signature, issuer, audience, scopes, claims and bounded verification admission on one route.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
jwt_auth:
  jwks_secret: phase3-jwks.json
  issuer: https://issuer.example.test
  audience: payments-api
  required_type: at+jwt
  algorithms:
    - RS256
  clock_skew_seconds: 5
  max_token_lifetime_seconds: 300
  required_scopes:
    - payments:read
  required_claims:
    - name: tenant
      exact: tenant-a
  verification_rate_limit:
    capacity: 1000
    refill_tokens_per_second: 1000
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-local-rate-limit">
<summary>Local route rate limit</summary>

Add a shard-local token bucket with explicit capacity and refill rate to one route.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
local_rate_limit:
  capacity: 2
  refill_tokens_per_second: 1
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-request-content">
<summary>Request-content policy</summary>

Constrain request body size and accepted media types before forwarding upstream.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
request_content:
  max_body_bytes: 8
  allowed_content_types:
    - application/json
    - application/problem+json
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-rewrite">
<summary>Upstream request rewrite</summary>

Rewrite the upstream authority and path prefix for one matched route.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
rewrite:
  host: orders.internal.test
  port: 9443
  path_prefix: /v2/
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-static-redirect">
<summary>Static redirect</summary>

Return a bounded redirect status and location components without contacting an upstream.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
redirect:
  status_code: 307
  path: /v2/orders
  query: source=legacy
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-upstream">
<summary>Proxied upstream route</summary>

Append a prefix route that forwards matching requests to a named cluster.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes` using `append-array-item` semantics:

```yaml
- name: default-route
  match:
    path_prefix: /
  cluster: local-upstream
```

</details>

<details id="example-route-weighted-clusters">
<summary>Weighted upstream clusters</summary>

Distribute one route deterministically across named clusters using positive integer weights.

Place this fragment at `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*` using `merge-object` semantics:

```yaml
weighted_clusters:
  - cluster: stable
    weight: 3
  - cluster: canary
    weight: 1
```

</details>

## Cross-field rules

- A route match selects exactly one of `path_exact`,
  `path_prefix`, or `safe_regex`.
- Every route selects exactly one action: `cluster`,
  `weighted_clusters`, `fixed_response`, or
  `redirect`.
- `api_key_auth` and `jwt_auth` are mutually
  exclusive on one route.
- Header transformations and rewrites require an upstream cluster action.
  WebSocket forwarding also requires a cluster action and
  `max_concurrent_requests_per_shard`.
- Downstream mTLS requires `require_client_certificate: true`
  and `trust_bundle_secret`. Without client-certificate
  enforcement, a downstream trust bundle is rejected.
- An upstream certificate chain and private key must be configured together.
  HTTP/2 upstream clusters require `upstream_tls`;
  `max_http2_streams_per_connection` is valid only for HTTP/2.
- A header or query matcher chooses exactly one of `exact` or
  `present`.
- CORS chooses either `allow_any_origin: true` or an
  `allowed_origins` list. Source-IP policy requires at least one
  allow or deny CIDR list. Request-content policy requires at least one bound.
- A `remove` header mutation carries no value; `set`
  and `append` require one.
- Redirect `scheme` and `host` are paired;
  `port` requires both. A rewrite cannot set both
  `path` and `path_prefix`.
- Schema-recognized syntax is not automatically a supported runtime feature.
  For example, the first OSS candidate supports downstream HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2;
  selecting `http3` is rejected by semantic validation.

Run [offline validation](../../how-to/validate-configuration/) after every edit.
Use [configuration diagnostics](../configuration-diagnostics/) to interpret a
rejection and [supported capabilities](../supported-capabilities/) before relying
on a protocol or operating mode.

## Parameter catalog

## Server identity and local management

These fields identify one gateway process and bind its local administration and metrics endpoints.

| YAML path | Parameter | Type | Direct presence | Constraints | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/server` | Server identity | `object` | Required | None at this structural level | Local node identity and administrative bind addresses for this gateway process. |
| `/server/admin_addr` | Admin address | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The local address used by the gateway administrative endpoint. |
| `/server/metrics_addr` | Metrics address | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The local address used to expose Prometheus metrics. |
| `/server/node_id` | Node ID | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The stable identity reported by this gateway node to management and observability surfaces. |

## Snapshot identity

These fields version the desired state compiled into one immutable runtime snapshot.

| YAML path | Parameter | Type | Direct presence | Constraints | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/snapshot` | Snapshot metadata | `object` | Required | None at this structural level | Version and identity metadata bound to the compiled immutable configuration artifact. |
| `/snapshot/generation` | Snapshot generation | `integer` | Required | minimum 1 | A positive operator-controlled generation used to order desired-state revisions. |
| `/snapshot/minimum_dataplane_version` | Minimum data-plane version | `string` | Optional | at least 1 character | The minimum BonVoyage data-plane version declared compatible with this snapshot. |
| `/snapshot/schema_version` | Configuration schema version | `integer` | Required | must be `1` | The configuration schema version interpreted by the installed compiler; contract v1 supports version 1. |
| `/snapshot/snapshot_id` | Snapshot ID | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The stable operator-visible identifier assigned to this desired-state snapshot. |

## Listeners

Listeners accept downstream connections, select protocol and virtual hosts, and optionally enforce TLS or trusted-proxy boundaries.

| YAML path | Parameter | Type | Direct presence | Constraints | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/listeners` | Listeners | `array<object>` | Required | at least 1 item | The non-empty set of downstream network listeners exposed by the gateway. |
| `/listeners/*/address` | Listener address | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The local network address on which this listener accepts downstream connections. |
| `/listeners/*/downstream_tls` | Downstream TLS | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | TLS certificate and optional client-authentication settings for this listener. |
| `/listeners/*/downstream_tls/certificate_chain_secret` | Server certificate secret | `string` | Required | validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing the listener certificate chain. |
| `/listeners/*/downstream_tls/private_key_secret` | Server private-key secret | `string` | Required | validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing the listener private key. |
| `/listeners/*/downstream_tls/require_client_certificate` | Require client certificate | `boolean` | Optional | None at this structural level | Whether the listener requires and verifies a downstream client certificate. |
| `/listeners/*/downstream_tls/trust_bundle_secret` | Client trust-bundle secret | `string` | Optional | validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing authorities trusted for downstream client certificates. |
| `/listeners/*/name` | Listener name | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The unique stable name of this listener within the snapshot. |
| `/listeners/*/port` | Listener port | `integer` | Required | 1 to 65535 | The TCP port on which this listener accepts downstream connections. |
| `/listeners/*/protocol` | Listener protocol | `string` | Required | one of `http1`, `http2`, `http3` | The downstream HTTP protocol accepted by this listener. |
| `/listeners/*/trusted_proxy` | Trusted proxy policy | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | The explicit proxy-network boundary allowed to supply trusted forwarded client identity. |
| `/listeners/*/trusted_proxy/trusted_cidrs` | Trusted proxy networks | `array<string>` | Required | 1 to 64 items; items must be unique | The bounded CIDR set whose forwarded client-address metadata may be trusted. |
| `/listeners/*/virtual_hosts` | Listener virtual hosts | `array<string>` | Required | at least 1 item | The names of virtual hosts bound to this listener. |

## Virtual hosts, routes, and policies

Virtual hosts select domains. Their ordered routes match requests, choose one action, and optionally apply bounded admission or transformation policies.

| YAML path | Parameter | Type | Direct presence | Constraints | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/virtual_hosts` | Virtual hosts | `array<object>` | Required | at least 1 item | The non-empty set of domain-routing tables available to listeners. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/domains` | Virtual-host domains | `array<string>` | Required | at least 1 item | The domain patterns matched by this virtual host. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/name` | Virtual-host name | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The unique stable virtual-host name referenced by listeners. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes` | Routes | `array<object>` | Required | at least 1 item | The ordered non-empty route table evaluated within this virtual host. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/api_key_auth` | API-key authentication | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional API-key admission policy evaluated before an upstream request is sent. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/api_key_auth/credentials_secret` | API-key credentials secret | `string` | Required | 1 to 128 characters; validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing the accepted API-key credential set. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/api_key_auth/header_name` | API-key header | `string` | Optional | 1 to 128 characters; validated syntax | The downstream HTTP header from which the API key is read. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cluster` | Route cluster | `string` | Optional | at least 1 character | The single named upstream cluster selected by this route. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors` | CORS policy | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional cross-origin request and response policy for this route. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/allow_any_origin` | Allow any origin | `boolean` | Optional | None at this structural level | Whether any syntactically valid origin is accepted by this CORS policy. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/allow_credentials` | Allow credentials | `boolean` | Optional | None at this structural level | Whether CORS responses permit downstream credentials under the configured origin policy. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/allowed_headers` | Allowed request headers | `array<string>` | Optional | at most 32 items; items must be unique | The bounded request-header names allowed by CORS preflight handling. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/allowed_methods` | Allowed CORS methods | `array<string>` | Required | 1 to 16 items; items must be unique | The HTTP methods allowed by this route's CORS policy. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/allowed_origins` | Allowed origins | `array<string>` | Optional | 1 to 32 items; items must be unique | The explicit origin values accepted when any-origin mode is disabled. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/exposed_headers` | Exposed response headers | `array<string>` | Optional | at most 32 items; items must be unique | The response-header names exposed to browser clients by CORS. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/cors/max_age_seconds` | Preflight maximum age | `integer` | Optional | 0 to 86400 | The maximum number of seconds a browser may cache a successful CORS preflight. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/fixed_response` | Fixed response | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | A gateway-generated response action that does not contact an upstream cluster. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/fixed_response/body` | Fixed-response body | `string` | Optional | None at this structural level | The optional response body returned by this fixed-response action. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/fixed_response/content_type` | Fixed-response content type | `string` | Optional | at least 1 character | The optional media type returned with this fixed response. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/fixed_response/status_code` | Fixed-response status | `integer` | Required | 200 to 599 | The HTTP status code returned by this fixed-response action. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/header_transformations` | Header transformations | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Ordered request and response header mutations for an upstream route. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/header_transformations/request` | Request header mutations | `array<object>` | Optional | at most 16 items | The ordered bounded mutations applied before forwarding an upstream request. |

| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect` | Redirect response | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | A gateway-generated HTTP redirect action that does not contact an upstream cluster. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect/host` | Redirect host | `string` | Optional | 1 to 253 characters; validated syntax | The optional normalized host used to construct the redirect target. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect/path` | Redirect path | `string` | Required | 1 to 4096 characters; validated syntax | The absolute non-network-path redirect target path. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect/port` | Redirect port | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 65535 | The optional TCP port included in the redirect authority. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect/query` | Redirect query | `string` | Optional | at most 4096 characters; validated syntax | The optional query component appended to the redirect target without a leading question mark. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect/scheme` | Redirect scheme | `string` | Optional | one of `http`, `https` | The optional HTTP or HTTPS scheme used with an explicit redirect host. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/redirect/status_code` | Redirect status | `integer` | Required | one of `301`, `302`, `303`, `307`, `308` | The supported 3xx HTTP status returned by this redirect action. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/request_content` | Request-content policy | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional request media-type and body-size admission rules for this route. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/request_content/allowed_content_types` | Allowed content types | `array<string>` | Optional | 1 to 16 items; items must be unique | The explicit media types accepted by this route's request-content policy. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/request_content/max_body_bytes` | Route body limit | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1073741824 | The maximum request-body size in bytes accepted by this route. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/rewrite` | Route rewrite | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional upstream authority or path rewriting applied after route selection. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/rewrite/host` | Rewritten host | `string` | Optional | 1 to 253 characters; validated syntax | The normalized upstream host used after this rewrite. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/rewrite/path` | Rewritten exact path | `string` | Optional | 1 to 4096 characters; validated syntax | The absolute path that replaces the complete matched request path. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/rewrite/path_prefix` | Rewritten path prefix | `string` | Optional | 1 to 4096 characters; validated syntax | The absolute prefix that replaces the matched route prefix while preserving the suffix. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/rewrite/port` | Rewritten port | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 65535 | The optional upstream authority port used with a rewritten host. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/source_ip_policy` | Source-IP policy | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional allow or deny CIDR admission based on the resolved downstream client address. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/source_ip_policy/allow_cidrs` | Allowed source networks | `array<string>` | Optional | 1 to 64 items; items must be unique | The CIDR set from which resolved client addresses are admitted. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/source_ip_policy/deny_cidrs` | Denied source networks | `array<string>` | Optional | 1 to 64 items; items must be unique | The CIDR set from which resolved client addresses are rejected. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/websocket` | WebSocket policy | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Enables bounded WebSocket upgrade and forwarding behavior for an upstream route. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/websocket/idle_timeout_ms` | WebSocket idle timeout | `integer` | Optional | 1000 to 3600000 | The maximum idle period in milliseconds for an upgraded WebSocket connection. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/weighted_clusters` | Weighted clusters | `array<object>` | Optional | 2 to 16 items | The bounded set of named clusters and relative weights used for deterministic traffic distribution. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/weighted_clusters/*/cluster` | Weighted cluster name | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The named upstream cluster represented by this weighted entry. |
| `/virtual_hosts/*/routes/*/weighted_clusters/*/weight` | Cluster weight | `integer` | Required | 1 to 4096 | The positive relative traffic weight assigned to this cluster. |

## Clusters, health, retries, and endpoints

Clusters describe upstream pools, connection limits, transport security, health behavior, retry budgets, and concrete endpoints.

| YAML path | Parameter | Type | Direct presence | Constraints | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/clusters` | Clusters | `array<object>` | Required | at least 1 item | The non-empty set of named upstream service pools available to routes. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health` | Active health checks | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional periodic HTTP health probing for endpoints in this cluster. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/expected_status_max` | Maximum healthy status | `integer` | Optional | 200 to 599 | The inclusive highest HTTP response status considered healthy by an active probe. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/expected_status_min` | Minimum healthy status | `integer` | Optional | 200 to 599 | The inclusive lowest HTTP response status considered healthy by an active probe. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/healthy_threshold` | Healthy threshold | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 100 | The consecutive successful probes required before an endpoint becomes healthy. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/host` | Health-check host | `string` | Optional | 1 to 253 characters | The HTTP Host or authority value used by active health-check requests. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/interval_ms` | Health-check interval | `integer` | Optional | 1000 to 300000 | The delay in milliseconds between scheduled active health probes. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/path` | Health-check path | `string` | Optional | 1 to 4096 characters; validated syntax | The absolute HTTP request path used for active health probes. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/timeout_ms` | Health-check timeout | `integer` | Optional | 100 to 10000 | The maximum time in milliseconds allowed for one active health probe. |
| `/clusters/*/active_health/unhealthy_threshold` | Unhealthy threshold | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 100 | The consecutive failed probes required before an endpoint becomes unhealthy. |
| `/clusters/*/connect_timeout_ms` | Connect timeout | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 60000 | The maximum time in milliseconds allowed to establish an upstream connection. |
| `/clusters/*/dns_refresh` | DNS refresh | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional bounded asynchronous hostname-resolution policy for cluster endpoints. |
| `/clusters/*/dns_refresh/refresh_interval_ms` | DNS refresh interval | `integer` | Optional | 1000 to 3600000 | The interval in milliseconds between accepted endpoint hostname refreshes. |
| `/clusters/*/dns_refresh/resolve_timeout_ms` | DNS resolution timeout | `integer` | Optional | 100 to 10000 | The maximum time in milliseconds allowed for one endpoint hostname resolution. |
| `/clusters/*/endpoints` | Endpoints | `array<object>` | Required | 1 to 4096 items | The non-empty set of upstream network destinations owned by this cluster. |
| `/clusters/*/endpoints/*/address` | Endpoint address | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The IP address or hostname used to connect to this upstream endpoint. |
| `/clusters/*/endpoints/*/name` | Endpoint name | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The unique stable name of this endpoint within its cluster. |
| `/clusters/*/endpoints/*/port` | Endpoint port | `integer` | Required | 1 to 65535 | The TCP port used to connect to this upstream endpoint. |
| `/clusters/*/endpoints/*/weight` | Endpoint weight | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 4096 | The relative endpoint selection weight used by a compatible load-balancing policy. |
| `/clusters/*/load_balancing_policy` | Load-balancing policy | `string` | Required | one of `round_robin`, `least_request`, `random` | The reviewed algorithm used to select an eligible endpoint for each request. |
| `/clusters/*/max_concurrent_requests_per_endpoint` | Endpoint request limit | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 2000000 | The maximum concurrent requests admitted to one endpoint before bounded rejection or alternate selection. |
| `/clusters/*/max_connections_per_shard` | Connections per shard | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000000 | The maximum shard-local upstream connections retained for this cluster. |
| `/clusters/*/max_http2_streams_per_connection` | HTTP/2 streams per connection | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000 | The maximum concurrent HTTP/2 streams admitted on one upstream connection. |
| `/clusters/*/max_pending_requests_per_shard` | Pending requests per shard | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000000 | The maximum shard-local requests allowed to wait for upstream capacity. |
| `/clusters/*/name` | Cluster name | `string` | Required | at least 1 character | The unique stable cluster name referenced by routes and weighted-cluster entries. |
| `/clusters/*/passive_health` | Passive health | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional endpoint ejection and recovery policy driven by proxied request outcomes. |
| `/clusters/*/passive_health/consecutive_failures` | Failure threshold | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 100 | The consecutive qualifying failures required before passive endpoint ejection. |
| `/clusters/*/passive_health/consecutive_successes` | Recovery threshold | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 100 | The consecutive successful observations required before passive recovery. |
| `/clusters/*/passive_health/ejection_time_ms` | Ejection duration | `integer` | Optional | 100 to 300000 | The bounded time in milliseconds an unhealthy endpoint remains passively ejected. |
| `/clusters/*/passive_health/max_ejection_percent` | Maximum ejection percentage | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 100 | The maximum percentage of cluster endpoints that passive health may eject at once. |
| `/clusters/*/protocol` | Upstream protocol | `string` | Optional | one of `http1`, `http2` | The application protocol BonVoyage uses when forwarding requests to this cluster. |
| `/clusters/*/retry` | Retry policy | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional bounded retry behavior for eligible failures and request methods. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/budget` | Retry budget | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Shard-local token and concurrency limits that contain retry amplification. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/budget/capacity` | Retry budget capacity | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000000 | The maximum number of retry tokens retained by the shard-local budget. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/budget/max_concurrent_retries_per_shard` | Concurrent retries per shard | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000000 | The maximum retries executing concurrently on one data-plane shard. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/budget/refill_tokens_per_second` | Retry token refill | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000000 | The number of retry-budget tokens replenished per second on each shard. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/max_attempts` | Maximum attempts | `integer` | Optional | 2 to 5 | The total bounded upstream attempts permitted for one eligible request. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/per_try_timeout_ms` | Per-try timeout | `integer` | Optional | 10 to 60000 | The maximum time in milliseconds allowed for each individual upstream attempt. |
| `/clusters/*/retry/retryable_methods` | Retryable methods | `array<string>` | Optional | 1 to 5 items; items must be unique | The explicit HTTP methods eligible for this cluster retry policy. |
| `/clusters/*/upstream_tls` | Upstream TLS | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | TLS server verification and optional client-certificate settings for this cluster. |
| `/clusters/*/upstream_tls/certificate_chain_secret` | Client certificate secret | `string` | Optional | validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing the client certificate chain used for upstream mTLS. |
| `/clusters/*/upstream_tls/private_key_secret` | Client private-key secret | `string` | Optional | validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing the private key used for upstream mTLS. |
| `/clusters/*/upstream_tls/server_name` | TLS server name | `string` | Required | 1 to 253 characters; validated syntax | The expected upstream server identity used for SNI and certificate verification. |
| `/clusters/*/upstream_tls/trust_bundle_secret` | Upstream trust-bundle secret | `string` | Required | validated syntax; deployment-secret filename only; never secret contents | The deployment-secret filename containing trusted certificate authorities for the upstream server. |

## Runtime limits

Runtime limits bound request sizes, timeouts, response metadata, idle connections, and downstream connection density.

| YAML path | Parameter | Type | Direct presence | Constraints | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/runtime_limits` | Runtime limits | `object` | Optional | None at this structural level | Optional global safety ceilings applied by the data plane for this snapshot. |
| `/runtime_limits/downstream_idle_timeout_ms` | Downstream idle timeout | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 3600000 | The maximum downstream connection idle period in milliseconds. |
| `/runtime_limits/max_downstream_connections_per_shard` | Downstream connections per shard | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1000000 | The maximum downstream connections admitted by one data-plane shard. |
| `/runtime_limits/max_request_body_bytes` | Maximum request body | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 1073741824 | The global maximum accepted downstream request-body size in bytes. |
| `/runtime_limits/max_request_header_bytes` | Maximum request headers | `integer` | Optional | 1024 to 1048576 | The global maximum accepted downstream request-header size in bytes. |
| `/runtime_limits/max_upstream_chunk_metadata_bytes` | Maximum chunk metadata | `integer` | Optional | 1024 to 1048576 | The maximum upstream chunk-metadata bytes retained while processing a response. |
| `/runtime_limits/max_upstream_response_header_bytes` | Maximum response headers | `integer` | Optional | 1024 to 1048576 | The maximum accepted upstream response-header size in bytes. |
| `/runtime_limits/request_timeout_ms` | Request timeout | `integer` | Optional | 1 to 300000 | The global maximum request lifetime in milliseconds unless a stricter boundary applies. |

## Authority and defaults

This page describes source syntax. Optional fields may receive safe compiler
defaults, but the formatter deliberately does not materialize those defaults
into YAML. Do not infer a default merely because a field is optional. Validate
with the exact installed release and inspect preview output before rollout.

The catalog does not prove that a gateway received, ACKed, or activated a
snapshot. Runtime confirmation remains a separate management and traffic test.
